ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, where $AB = 3$ and $BC = 4$, connect $BD$ and draw the bisector of $\angle CBD$ intersecting $CD$ at point $E$. What is the length of $CE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct EH$\perp$BD at H, as shown in the figure,\\
since quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle,\\
therefore AB＝CD＝3, BC＝AD＝4, $\angle$C＝$90^\circ$,\\
therefore BD＝$\sqrt{BC^{2}+CD^{2}}$＝5,\\
since BE bisects $\angle$CBD,\\
therefore $\angle$EBC＝$\angle$EBH,\\
In $\triangle$EBH and $\triangle$EBC,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle EHB=\angle C=90^\circ\\
\angle EBH=\angle EBC\\
BE=BE
\end{array}\right.$,\\
therefore $\triangle$EBH$\cong$$\triangle$EBC,\\
therefore BC＝BH＝4, EC＝EH, let EC＝EH＝x,\\
In $\triangle$DEH,\\
since DE$^{2}$＝DH$^{2}$+EH$^{2}$,\\
therefore $(3−x)^{2}$＝$1^{2}$+$x^{2}$,\\
therefore x＝$\boxed{\frac{4}{3}}$,\\
therefore CE＝$\frac{4}{3}$.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates and the vector direction of an angle bisector. From the diagram, place B=(0,0), C=(4,0), D=(4,3), matching the rectangle orientation with BC horizontal and CD vertical. The ray BC has unit direction (1,0). The ray BD has direction (4,3), whose length is 5, so its unit direction is (4/5,3/5). The internal angle bisector from B has direction equal to the sum of the two unit direction vectors: (1,0)+(4/5,3/5)=(9/5,3/5), which has slope (3/5)/(9/5)=1/3. Thus BE has equation y=x/3. ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $EH \perp BD$ at $H$, as shown in the figure,\\
since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle,\\
therefore $AB=CD=3$, $BC=AD=4$, $\angle C=90^\circ$,\\
therefore $BD=\sqrt{BC^{2}+CD^{2}}=5$,\\
since $BE$ bisects $\angle CBD$,\\
therefore $\angle EBC=\angle EBH$,\\
In $\triangle EBH$ and $\triangle EBC$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle EHB=\angle C=90^\circ\\
\angle EBH=\angle EBC\\
BE=BE
\end{array}\right.$,\\
therefore $\triangle EBH\cong\triangle EBC$,\\
therefore $BC=BH=4$, $EC=EH$, let $EC=EH=x$,\\
In $\triangle DEH$,\\
since $DE^{2}=DH^{2}+EH^{2}$,\\
therefore $(3-x)^{2}=1^{2}+x^{2}$,\\
therefore $x=\boxed{\frac{4}{3}}$,\\
therefore $CE=\frac{4}{3}$.
